interface Box { a: boolean; b: boolean; c: boolean; d: boolean }

declare function f(): void;

// cycPos has nine ifs: cyclomatic 1 + 9 = 10.
function cycPos(x: Box): void {
  if (x.a) { f(); }
  if (x.b) { f(); }
  if (x.c) { f(); }
  if (x.d) { f(); }
  if (x.a) { f(); }
  if (x.b) { f(); }
  if (x.c) { f(); }
  if (x.d) { f(); }
  if (x.a) { f(); }
}

// cycNeg has eight ifs: cyclomatic 9.
function cycNeg(x: Box): void {
  if (x.a) { f(); }
  if (x.b) { f(); }
  if (x.c) { f(); }
  if (x.d) { f(); }
  if (x.a) { f(); }
  if (x.b) { f(); }
  if (x.c) { f(); }
  if (x.d) { f(); }
}

// nestPos nests four ifs: depth 4, one bump, cyclomatic 5.
function nestPos(x: Box): void {
  if (x.a) {
    if (x.b) {
      if (x.c) {
        if (x.d) {
          f();
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

// nestNeg nests three ifs: depth 3, one bump, cyclomatic 4.
function nestNeg(x: Box): void {
  if (x.a) {
    if (x.b) {
      if (x.c) {
        f();
      }
    }
  }
}

// bumpsPos has two separate top-level blocks that reach depth 2.
function bumpsPos(x: Box): void {
  if (x.a) {
    if (x.b) {
      f();
    }
  }
  f();
  if (x.c) {
    if (x.d) {
      f();
    }
  }
}

// bumpsNeg has one nested block and one flat if.
function bumpsNeg(x: Box): void {
  if (x.a) {
    if (x.b) {
      f();
    }
  }
  if (x.c) {
    f();
  }
}

// boolPos has three boolean operators in one condition.
function boolPos(x: Box): void {
  if (x.a && x.b && x.c || x.d) {
    f();
  }
}

// boolNeg has two boolean operators in one condition.
function boolNeg(x: Box): void {
  if (x.a && x.b || x.c) {
    f();
  }
}

// argsPos has five parameters.
function argsPos(a: Box, b: Box, c: Box, d: Box, e: Box): void {}

// argsNeg has four parameters.
function argsNeg(a: Box, b: Box, c: Box, d: Box): void {}

// primPos has four parameters, three of them primitive (75%).
function primPos(a: string, b: number, c: boolean, d: Box): void {}

// primNeg has four parameters, two of them primitive (50%).
function primNeg(a: string, b: number, c: Box, d: Box): void {}

// primFew has three primitive parameters: too few for the smell.
function primFew(a: string, b: number, c: boolean): void {}

// params: this is not a parameter; optional and rest parameters are.
function params(this: Box, a?: string, ...rest: number[]): void {}

// constructs uses every ECMAScript decision point once; default is not one.
function constructs(a: number, xs: number[], x: Box): number {
  if (x.a && x.b || x.c) {
    a++;
  } else if (x.d) {
    a--;
  }
  for (let i = 0; i < a; i++) {}
  for (const e of xs) {}
  for (const k in x) {}
  while (a > 100) { a--; }
  do { a++; } while (a < 3);
  switch (a) {
    case 1:
    case 2:
      break;
    default:
      break;
  }
  try { f(); } catch (e) { f(); }
  const t = x.a ? 1 : 2;
  const u = x.b ?? x.c;
  a ||= 1;
  a &&= 2;
  a ??= 3;
  return a;
}

// elseIf is a chain on one level.
function elseIf(x: Box): void {
  if (x.a) {
    f();
  } else if (x.b) {
    f();
  } else if (x.c) {
    f();
  } else {
    f();
  }
}

const arrow = (y: Box): void => {
  if (y.a) { f(); }
};

class Service {
  run(x: Box): void {
    if (x.a) { f(); }
  }

  field = (x: Box): void => {
    if (x.b) { f(); }
  };
}

// closures: the callbacks are anonymous and count toward the function; run is
// a named closure and a unit of its own; inner is a nested function.
function closures(x: Box, items: Box[]): void {
  const run = () => {
    if (x.a) { f(); }
  };
  items.forEach((item) => {
    if (item.b) { f(); }
  });
  items.map(function (item) {
    for (const k in item) { f(); }
    return item;
  });
  function inner(): void {
    if (x.c) { f(); }
  }
}
